page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware-level features such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI), AES cryptography, and virtualization. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the n2-standard-2 occupies the lower tiers of performance. Its stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 1398.19 is in the bottom 25%, while its multi-core score of 1837.38 falls into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block speeds at 13.8 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 11.79 GB/sec, both placing in the bottom 10%. However, single-threaded gzip compression shows average performance at 23.81 GB/sec. Other tests, including Geekbench multi-core (1333.0) and Passmark database operations (731.04), consistently rank in the bottom 10% of tested hardware.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-standard-2 provides a balanced resource allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, making it an entry-level option for workloads that do not require high computational density or high-speed memory access. Given its lower performance profile in multi-core processing, ray tracing, and database operations, this instance is suited for lightweight general-purpose tasks, basic web serving, single-threaded file compression, or development environments rather than resource-intensive production databases or data science jobs.
